{{ElectionsOH}}

The '''2022 Ohio Secretary of State election''' was held on November 8, 2022, to elect the [[Secretary of State of Ohio]].  [[Incumbent]] [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] [[Frank LaRose]] won re-election to a second term.

==Republican primary==
===Candidates===
====Nominee====
*[[Frank LaRose]], incumbent [[Ohio Secretary of State|Secretary of State]]<ref name=LaRose>{{cite web|url=https://spectrumnews1.com/oh/columbus/news/2021/05/17/frank-larose-is-re-running-for-secretary-of-state|title=Frank LaRose announces reelection bid for Ohio secretary of state|work=[[Spectrum News]]|last=Taylor|first=Lydia|date=May 17, 2021|access-date=December 21, 2021}}</ref><ref name=PetVer/>

====Eliminated in primary====
*[[John Adams (Ohio politician)|John Adams]], former [[Ohio House of Representatives|state representative]] from the 85th district (2007–2014)<ref>{{Cite web|last=Bischoff|first=Laura|url=https://www.dispatch.com/story/news/2021/08/23/gop-primary-john-adams-running-against-ohio-secretary-state-larose/8242596002/|title=Former Ohio lawmaker with doubts about Joe Biden's win wants to run Ohio elections|date=August 23, 2021|work=[[Columbus Dispatch]]}}</ref><ref name=PetVer>{{Cite news|date=February 16, 2022|title=CANDIDATE PETITION VERIFICATIONS FOR THE 2022 PRIMARY ELECTION RELEASED|work=Ohio Secretary of State|url=https://www.ohiosos.gov/media-center/press-releases/2022/2022-02-16/|access-date=February 27, 2022}}</ref>

====Disqualified====
*Terpsichore “Tore” Maras-Lindeman, podcaster<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.toledoblade.com/local/politics/2022/02/01/controversial-podcaster-files-to-run-for-ohio-s-top-elections-office/stories/20220201105|title=Controversial podcaster files to run for Ohio's top elections office|work=[[The Blade (Toledo, Ohio)|The Blade]]|last=Provance|first=Jim|date=February 1, 2022|access-date=February 4, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|date=February 3, 2022|title=FILINGS FOR THE 2022 PRIMARY ELECTION RELEASED|work=Ohio Secretary of State|url=https://www.ohiosos.gov/media-center/press-releases/2022/2022-02-03/|access-date=February 4, 2022|archive-date=February 4, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220204045311/https://www.ohiosos.gov/media-center/press-releases/2022/2022-02-03/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=PetVer/> ''(running as an Independent)''
